content.user_title: Build NixOS Modules with Home Manager Patterns
content.value_statement: NixOS and Home Manager module setup can be repetitive and error-prone. This skill gives concise patterns for packages, modules, and imports.
actual_capabilities: Shows standard directories for Home Manager modules, NixOS modules, hosts, and the home entry point.
Provides a package list pattern using pkgs, lib.optionals, and platform checks.
Provides a simple Home Manager module skeleton with package and config file examples.
Shows how to import a Home Manager module from home/default.nix.
Helps keep Nix configuration examples short and consistent.
limitations: Covers concise module patterns, not a full NixOS architecture guide.
Does not include flake setup, lock file maintenance, or channel management.
Does not run Nix evaluation, formatting, or rebuild commands.
Does not cover secret management or complex service hardening.

use_cases.title: Create a Home Manager Module
use_cases.description: Draft a small module that adds packages and writes user configuration files.

use_cases.title: Organize System Configuration
use_cases.description: Place NixOS modules, Home Manager modules, and host files in predictable directories.

use_cases.title: Review Package Patterns
use_cases.description: Check whether package additions use clear lists and platform-specific conditionals.

prompt_templates.title: Add User Packages
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the nix-patterns skill to add these Home Manager packages: [packages]. Keep the module structure simple.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Small Module
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the nix-patterns skill to draft a Home Manager module for [program]. Include packages and one configuration file.

prompt_templates.title: Add Platform Conditions
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the nix-patterns skill to add [package] only on x86_64-linux while keeping shared packages available everywhere.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Module Layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the nix-patterns skill to reorganize this Nix configuration into home modules, NixOS modules, host files, and imports.

output_examples.input: I need a Home Manager module for a desktop app with one settings file.
output_examples.output: A concise module plan with the package list, the user config file location, and the import location.

output_examples.input: I want one package only on x86_64-linux systems.
output_examples.output: A package list recommendation that separates shared packages from platform-specific packages.

output_examples.input: My repository has mixed NixOS and Home Manager files.
output_examples.output: A directory layout recommendation that separates user modules, system modules, host configuration, and the main home entry point.

best_practices: Keep Home Manager modules focused on user packages and user configuration files.
Use platform conditionals when a package is only valid for one system type.
Import modules from a clear entry point so configuration flow stays easy to review.
anti_patterns: Mixing host-specific settings into reusable Home Manager modules.
Adding platform-specific packages to shared package lists without conditionals.
Creating modules without adding them to the appropriate import list.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps create and edit concise NixOS and Home Manager module patterns.

faq.question: Can it run nixos-rebuild or home-manager commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides guidance and patterns, but it does not execute system commands.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is this a complete NixOS tutorial?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on small module examples and directory patterns.

faq.question: Does it include Home Manager examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes package lists, user configuration files, and a module import example.

faq.question: Can it validate whether Nix code evaluates?
faq.answer: No. Use Nix tooling to evaluate, format, and test generated configuration changes.
